findings: Root cause: users table has no deleted_at column (only is_deleted boolean), but excludeDeleted() in genericSearch.ts hardcodes .where('deleted_at','IS',null) for every table — a column that simply doesn't exist on users.

The ORM's unknownColumnMode:'silent-skip' (enabled for all search endpoints) converts that invalid column reference into a silent no-op instead of an error, so the soft-delete filter is dropped entirely for users searches while working correctly for orders (which does have deleted_at) — this is the direct mechanism producing the reported bug.

Design flaw: silent-skip was configured to tolerate genuinely optional filters referencing missing columns, but it applies identically to excludeDeleted()'s mandatory correctness/visibility filter — there is no way in this setup to distinguish 'safe to skip' from 'must never be skipped,' so a config meant to prevent 500s instead silently converts a security/compliance-relevant filter into wrong results, which is a worse failure mode than the 500 it was avoiding.

Systemic/structural risk beyond this one bug: silent-skip is applied globally across all search endpoints, and search()'s q.where(filters) also passes arbitrary caller-supplied filters straight through per table — any other shared filter or caller-supplied filter that references a column absent from a given table's schema will silently drop rather than error, so this class of bug is not limited to soft-delete and can recur wherever table schemas diverge.

Underlying architecture smell: orders and users use two incompatible soft-delete conventions (nullable deleted_at timestamp vs. NOT NULL is_deleted boolean with no timestamp) with no shared/enforced soft-delete contract across tables, which is what let excludeDeleted() be written as if one convention applied uniformly.

Detection gap: this was only caught via a support report rather than by any test or monitoring around per-table soft-delete filtering or unknown-column-skip events, indicating the generic search layer lacks coverage verifying that excludeDeleted() actually applies to every table it's used against.

Fix should address the root cause, not just add a users.deleted_at column: excludeDeleted() (or equivalent) needs to be made table-aware (branch on each table's actual delete-marker column) and/or the schemas should be unified on one soft-delete convention; silent-skip should not be relied upon for filters that are correctness/security-critical.
